title: Why Strict, Fair, Compassionate Accountability Makes You Popular With Students y-makes-you-popular-with-students/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin describes the surprise many teachers feel when consistent accountability makes them among the most popular teachers at school, not merely respected but genuinely well-liked. He attributes this to three effects: students respect the rare integrity of a teacher who does what they say they'll do, they appreciate a peaceful classroom free of interruption and bullying, and they feel liberated once they realize that agreed-upon consequences are the only consequences and that enforcement is never personal. This combination, he argues, frees students to take responsibility for their own mistakes and strengthens their trust and affection for the teacher. He cautions that this only works if the teacher enforces the classroom management plan like a neutral referee rather than a judge, without added lectures, scolding, or personal input, concluding that faithful accountability, done this way, ultimately earns students' love rather than resentment.
points: Consistent, promised accountability tends to make teachers not just respected but genuinely popular with students.
Students respect rare integrity—teachers who reliably follow through on what they say they'll do.
A peaceful, interruption-free classroom is deeply appreciated by students who have experienced chaotic alternatives elsewhere.
Students feel liberated once they know consequences are the only consequences and enforcement is never personal.
Enforcement must be delivered like a neutral referee, without lecturing, scolding, or added personal commentary, for the effect to hold.
quotes: You see, when you consistently hold students accountable according to rules and expectations you lay out ahead of time, it makes you the most popular teacher at school.
So when students meet someone that actually does what they say they’re going to do, they can’t help but be affected.

Once you prove to your students that the agreed-upon consequences are the only consequences, and that you’re not going to lecture, scold, glare, admonish, or otherwise take their misbehavior personally, it frees them to truly enjoy your class.
This, in turn, safeguards your relationship with them. In fact, it makes their trust and belief in you, as well as your likability, even stronger.
You must enforce your consequences like a referee rather than a judge.
So that your students will not only never hold your faithful accountability against you. They’ll love you for it.
